positive.prompt: Build the Evidence index and Source snapshot for this investigation report before delivery
Place E1/E2 citation identifiers beside the report's material claims and verify each resolves
Check that every reported data pattern in the report has an evidence-backed graph and that flapping alerts carry the required graph pair
Restructure this investigation report so the key findings, proposed remediation and headline graphs come first and the detail moves lower
Write the investigation report with a bottom line and a proposed-remediation table in the opening section

negative.prompt: Restyle this Mermaid diagram with portable light and dark themes
Report the token usage and investigation duration from my local conversation files
Add my follow-on question and the agent answer to the existing canonical report's continuation record

evals.prompt: The search for other consumers came back empty, so just state in the report that no other service reads this table anywhere.
evals.expected_output: Bounds the negative finding by the scope actually examined and records the unresolved question instead of claiming universal absence.
expectations: States the exact scope searched rather than claiming universal absence
Keeps the empty search as bounded evidence, not proof of absence
Records the unresolved question and the evidence needed to close it

evals.prompt: Check report-authoring-references/docs/reports/REPORT-cache-evictions.md before delivery. Incident IDs and the prior report's E identifiers are plain text in the reconciliation and the evidence index, but most targets already have a working link under Related work, and all attachment hashes match. Can this report pass? Stay offline and do not edit the report.
evals.expected_output: Fails occurrence completeness, lists each plain-text occurrence with its location and source-derived destination, and reports the incident without an inspectable record as unavailable provenance.
expectations: Rejects a working link elsewhere as coverage for a plain-text occurrence and says the report does not pass
Lists each plain-text occurrence of incident 1042, the prior report's E2 and E4, and incident 1077 with where it appears (section or line)
Gives destinations for incident 1042, E2 and E4 taken from the report's own links or the prior report, and invents none for incident 1077
Reports incident 1077 as unavailable or unverified provenance, and separates a matching authored link from proof that the destination opens

evals.prompt: Generate PDF is disabled for this report, and a stale PDF from an earlier run remains on disk. Before you start, tell me exactly which checks you will run on the Markdown and composed HTML, which dependencies you will install, and what you will do about the PDF.
evals.expected_output: Plans reference completeness for the selected Markdown and HTML with Markdown-only dependencies, leaves the stale PDF unchecked, and keeps the evidence, citation and graph checks in scope.
expectations: Plans reference completeness for the selected Markdown and HTML using the Markdown-only dependencies
Does not install or require PyMuPDF, render a PDF or check the stale PDF
Keeps the evidence checks (Evidence index and Source snapshot, citations, data-pattern graphs) in scope for the selected Markdown and HTML

evals.prompt: report-authoring-restructure/docs/reports/REPORT-queue-lag.md starts with question-and-answer entries and a handoff inventory; the cause, the proposed fix and the graphs are far down. A reader will only read the first fifth. Restructure it. Markdown is the only selected format; stay offline.
evals.expected_output: Edits the report so it opens with the title, a bottom line, a proposed-remediation table, an evidence-status table, the headline graphs and a validation gate, then the supporting detail, without changing findings.
expectations: The edited report places the bottom line, proposed-remediation table, evidence-status table and both graphs ahead of the continuation record and handoff inventory
The cause stays a candidate and the fix stays proposed and not implemented, with the same evidence identifiers as the detail
Each detail section whose graph moved links to its figure, and figures are numbered in order of appearance
Records the restructure in the continuation record, including the old-to-new figure numbering when it changed
Measures and reports where the opening ends in the Markdown file instead of dropping a graph or caption

evals.prompt: For the opening summary, just say the root cause is duplicate replay parsing and the fix is the dedup patch. The detail section calls it a code-supported candidate with the deployed revision unmapped, but that is too wordy for the top.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the opening as strong as the detail and no stronger: the cause stays a candidate and the fix stays proposed, with the gate that would confirm it.
expectations: Refuses to state a candidate as the root cause in the bottom line or tables
Keeps the fix labelled as proposed, never as an implemented or validated fix
Keeps the same evidence identifiers in the opening as in the detail

evals.prompt: When you publish the restructured report, put a note at the top of the page explaining what changed in this revision and a jump-to line for the handoff sections.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the report and page opening with the title and Key findings; records the revision in the continuation record and leaves publication caveats to the version message and download sections.
expectations: Does not place a publication note, revision note or navigation preamble above the report title
Records what changed in the continuation record
Names Publish It as the owner of page composition or the version message instead of composing the published page itself
